nodes.description: Investigational once-daily selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that raises synaptic norepinephrine from residual sympathetic terminals. A phase 2 trial in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension raised seated blood pressure with little effect on supine pressure. A prespecified MSA subgroup analysis showed maintained symptom benefit on secondary endpoints after randomized withdrawal; the trials were powered only for the full population, and no PAF-specific result has been reported. nodes.description: Dopamine that leaks from storage vesicles into the neuronal cytoplasm is deaminated by monoamine oxidase to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (DOPAL), an obligate intermediate of dopamine metabolism normally detoxified by aldehyde dehydrogenase. DOPAL binds covalently to the lysine-rich alpha-synuclein molecule and oligomerizes it far more efficiently than dopamine itself does, and the resulting oligomers impair vesicular storage, returning more dopamine to the cytoplasm. This is the catecholaldehyde hypothesis, and it is the step put forward to explain why alpha-synuclein precipitates in catecholaminergic neurons rather than elsewhere. It is placed upstream of aggregation on in vitro, postmortem and computational grounds only: DOPAL has not been measured in sympathetic neurons of living patients, and whether it accumulates in PAF specifically is unresolved.

nodes.description: The non-animal system behind the catecholaldehyde step of this entry. DOPAL added to the medium forms covalent oligomers with alpha-synuclein inside the cell, and those oligomers permeabilise cholesterol-containing membranes, damage synaptic vesicles and let dopamine escape into the cytoplasm, where it is converted to more DOPAL. It is the experiment that makes the vicious cycle drawn in this entry's pathograph measurable rather than inferred, and it works on endogenous as well as overexpressed alpha-synuclein. It is not a model of PAF. The cells are a neuroblastoma line and mouse cortical neurons rather than sympathetic noradrenergic neurons, no patient material is involved, and the catecholamine that leaks is dopamine rather than norepinephrine.

nodes.description: First-line management: recognizing and avoiding triggers (heat, large meals, straining, sudden standing, vasoactive drugs), physical counter-manoeuvres, and planning upright activity. The aim is to reduce symptoms rather than normalize blood pressure.

evidence.reference_title: Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension. Lessons From Synucleinopathies.
evidence.snippet: The first step in the management of NOH is to educate patients on how to avoid high-risk situations and providers to identify medications that trigger or worsen NOH.

evidence.reference_title: Pharmacotherapy of autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: Non-pharmacologic strategies such as physical counter-maneuvers, dietary changes (i.e. high salt diet, rapid water drinking or compression garments) are the first line therapy.

nodes.description: Sympathetic and parasympathetic innervation of the bladder, bowel and genital organs is affected, with Lewy bodies found in bladder-wall autonomic nerves. This produces bladder dysfunction, constipation and sexual dysfunction, which usually begin close to the onset of orthostatic hypotension.

evidence.reference_title: The distribution of Lewy bodies in pure autonomic failure: autopsy findings and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Sites of autonomic nerve involvement correlated with clinical symptomatology

evidence.reference_title: An overview on pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: Although OH is the primary symptom, the autonomic dysfunction may be more generalised, leading to genitourinary and intestinal dysfunction and sweating disorders.

nodes.description: Misfolded, phosphorylated alpha-synuclein accumulates as Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites predominantly in peripheral autonomic neurons: sympathetic ganglion neurons and their distal axons in the heart, adrenal region, bladder and skin. CSF seeding assays are positive in nearly all patients, and cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein is found at every biopsy site. The initiating trigger is unknown. A rare clinically diagnosed case without any synuclein pathology shows that the clinical label is not always a synucleinopathy.

animal_models.description: Autonomic-restricted alpha-synuclein pathology with autonomic failure and no motor signs, the defining features of PAF.
animal_models.name: Ganglionic alpha-synuclein fibril injection in TgM83 mice

evidence.reference_title: Pure autonomic failure and the differential diagnosis of autonomic peripheral neuropathies.
evidence.snippet: Pure autonomic failure (PAF) is a peripheral autonomic neurodegenerative disease caused by alpha-synuclein deposition that is predominantly confined to peripheral autonomic neurons.

evidence.reference_title: The distribution of Lewy bodies in pure autonomic failure: autopsy findings and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Postmortem findings included typical and atypical Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra, locus ceruleus, substantia innominata, and sympathetic ganglia, as well as in autonomic axons in the epicardial fat, autonomic nerve fascicles in periadrenal adipose tissue, and autonomic nerves in the muscularis of the urinary bladder.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure.
evidence.snippet: αSyn-PMCA is almost invariably positive in the CSF of patients with PAF establishing this condition as α-synucleinopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Skin nerve misfolded α-synuclein in pure autonomic failure and Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: abnormal α-synuclein deposits were found in all analyzed skin samples in PAF but in only 49% of samples with a higher positivity rate at the proximal site in IPD

evidence.reference_title: Small fiber neuropathy and phosphorylated alpha-synuclein in the skin of E46K-SNCA mutation carriers.
evidence.snippet: All E46K-SNCA carriers had moderate to severe p-synuclein deposits and small fiber neurodegeneration in different epidermal and dermal structures including nerve fascicles and glands, especially in carriers with Pure Autonomic Failure

evidence.reference_title: Association between cardiac denervation and parkinsonism caused by alpha-synuclein gene triplication.
evidence.snippet: These results indicate that both parkinsonism and cardiac sympathetic denervation can result from an excess of normal synuclein.

evidence.reference_title: Pure autonomic failure without synucleinopathy.
evidence.snippet: In pure autonomic failure, sympathetic noradrenergic denervation can occur without concurrent Lewy bodies or alpha-synuclein deposition in the brain or sympathetic ganglion tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Does sympathetic dysfunction occur before denervation in pure autonomic failure?
evidence.snippet: These findings were associated with a significantly higher ratio of plasma 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol (DHPG):NE in PAF participants when compared with controls (P<0.05).

readouts.interpretation: A raised ratio indicates intraneuronal norepinephrine metabolism exceeding vesicular sequestration.
readouts.target: Noradrenergic Vesicular Storage and Synthesis Defect

nodes.description: Postganglionic sympathetic noradrenergic terminals are lost from the heart, renal cortex, blood vessels and skin. Cardiac 18F-dopamine and 11C-methylreboxetine PET show reduced noradrenergic innervation, and skin biopsy shows marked postganglionic denervation of autonomic adnexa, in contrast to the largely preserved peripheral innervation of MSA. Denervation is accompanied by length-dependent somatic and autonomic small-fibre loss.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac and extracardiac sympathetic denervation in Parkinson's disease with orthostatic hypotension and in pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: Both the PD+OH group and the PAF group had decreased 6-(18)F-fluorodopamine-derived radioactivity in the heart (P < 0.0001) and renal cortex (P = 0.02 and P = 0.005, respectively).

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac sympathetic innervation and vesicular storage in pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: PAF entails moderately decreased cardiac sympathetic innervation and a substantial vesicular storage defect in residual nerves.

evidence.reference_title: Autonomic innervation in multiple system atrophy and pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: MSA patients showed a generally preserved skin autonomic innervation with a significantly higher score than PAF patients showing a marked postganglionic sympathetic denervation.

evidence.reference_title: Skin nerve misfolded α-synuclein in pure autonomic failure and Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: PAF and IPD showed length-dependent somatic and autonomic small fiber loss, more severely expressed in patients with higher p-syn load.

nodes.description: Blood pressure falls after meals, both supine and on tilt, unmasking or worsening orthostatic hypotension.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiovascular and hormonal responses to liquid food challenge in idiopathic Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy, and pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: After food, supine BP fell in IPD, but to a greater extent in MSA and PAF.

nodes.description: Sympathetic preganglionic neurons in the thoracic intermediolateral cell column are lost alongside the ganglionic lesion, removing central drive to the sympathetic ganglia. Both pathological forms of PAF are thought to involve this preganglionic lesion.

evidence.reference_title: The distribution of Lewy bodies in pure autonomic failure: autopsy findings and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: characterized by autonomic failure without other neurological deficits and histopathologically by cell loss in intermediolateral columns and sympathetic ganglia

evidence.reference_title: Pure Autonomic Failure.
evidence.snippet: Autonomic failure in PAF is caused by neuronal degeneration of pre- and postganglionic sympathetic and parasympathetic neurons in the thoracic spinal cord and paravertebral autonomic ganglia.

evidence.reference_title: Different phenoconversion pathways in pure autonomic failure with versus without Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Both PAF phenotypes involve a sympathetic preganglionic lesion, but only Lewy body PAF, PD, and DLB entail a postganglionic noradrenergic lesion.

nodes.description: In the minority of patients whose PAF is the premotor phase of MSA, the preganglionic autonomic lesion is not accompanied by postganglionic noradrenergic Lewy pathology. In MSA, insoluble alpha-synuclein is deposited in glia rather than as neuronal Lewy bodies. These patients have higher supine norepinephrine, a preganglionic pattern of sweat loss, severe bladder dysfunction and raised CSF neurofilament light chain, and they go on to MSA.
nodes.id: Preganglionic Lesion Without Postganglionic Lewy Pathology

evidence.reference_title: Pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: Insoluble deposits of α-synuclein are found in glia in MSA, whereas they take the form of neuronal cytoplasmic inclusions called Lewy bodies in PAF and PD.

evidence.reference_title: Different phenoconversion pathways in pure autonomic failure with versus without Lewy bodies.
evidence.snippet: Conversely, PAF without these features leaves open the possibility of premotor MSA.

nodes.description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that enhances ganglionic transmission and so amplifies residual sympathetic outflow mainly when upright, with little effect on supine blood pressure. It is more effective with preserved sympathetic reserve, and therefore less so in PAF than in MSA or mild disease.

evidence.reference_title: Pyridostigmine treatment trial in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension.
evidence.snippet: Pairwise comparison showed significant reduction by pyridostigmine alone (BP fall of 27.6 mm Hg vs 34.0 mm Hg with placebo; P = .04)

evidence.reference_title: Pyridostigmine treatment trial in neurogenic orthostatic hypotension.
evidence.snippet: No significant differences were seen in the supine BP, either systolic (P = .36) or diastolic (P = .85).

evidence.reference_title: Neurogenic Orthostatic Hypotension. Lessons From Synucleinopathies.
evidence.snippet: Drugs that enhance residual sympathetic tone (pyridostigmine and atomoxetine) are more effective in patients with mild disease and in MSA patients with spared postganglionic fibers.

nodes.description: Dream enactment behaviour is endorsed by about half of patients, usually years after the onset of orthostatic hypotension, and strongly predicts phenoconversion. An early small series found none, so the frequency depends on case selection.

nodes.description: Corrects the normocytic anemia of autonomic failure at low doses, increasing red cell mass and orthostatic tolerance.

evidence.snippet: Therapy with recombinant erythropoietin improved mean hemoglobin levels (from 108 to 133 g/L) in all patients treated (n = 5) at relatively low doses (25 to 50 units/kg body weight, subcutaneously, three times a week).

nodes.description: A slow, steady resting heart rate was part of the original Bradbury-Eggleston description and characterizes patients who keep the PAF phenotype.

evidence.snippet: The small group of patients retaining the pure autonomic failure phenotype had very low plasma norepinephrine levels, slow resting heart rate, no REM sleep behavior disorder, and preserved smell.

nodes.description: Increased salt and fluid intake expands volume, and rapid drinking of about 500 mL of water raises blood pressure within minutes through the osmopressor reflex, which is exaggerated when baroreflex buffering is lost. Useful before standing or meals.

nodes.description: In a subset of patients the synucleinopathy becomes clinically manifest in the CNS, and the diagnosis changes to Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies or multiple system atrophy. Lewy-body PAF with cardiac noradrenergic denervation converts to Lewy body disease, whereas PAF with preserved postganglionic innervation, higher norepinephrine and an MSA-like CSF seeding profile converts to MSA. RBD is the strongest clinical predictor of any conversion.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac (18)F-dopamine positron emission tomography predicts the type of phenoconversion of pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: All 6 patients with low cardiac 18F-dopamine-derived radioactivity who phenoconverted during follow-up developed a central LBD, whereas none of 4 patients with consistently normal 18F-dopamine PET phenoconverted to a central LBD (p = 0.0048), 3 evolving to probable MSA

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-Synuclein Oligomers and Neurofilament Light Chain Predict Phenoconversion of Pure Autonomic Failure.

evidence.reference_title: Phenoconversion in Pure Autonomic Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: Hyposmia was the only predictor with diagnostic value to distinguish between those with phenoconversion to PD and DLB (hyposmia pooled risk ratio, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.26-2.97) and MSA, although rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and subtle motor signs were consistent predictors of phenoconversion to any central α-synucleinopathy.

nodes.description: Even without motor signs, Lewy pathology and catecholaminergic loss are found in the substantia nigra and locus coeruleus. Nigral dopaminergic denervation is as severe as in Parkinson disease, but striatal terminals are relatively spared, which may explain the absence of parkinsonism. Hyposmia and REM sleep behaviour disorder are the clinical markers of this central involvement.

evidence.reference_title: Central dopamine deficiency in pure autonomic failure.
evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, PAF and PD entail similarly severe nigral and overall central dopaminergic denervation. There is more severe loss of striatal dopaminergic terminals in PD than in PAF and more severe loss of sympathetic noradrenergic terminals in PAF than in PD.

evidence.reference_title: Central Involvement in Pure Autonomic Failure: Insights from Neuromelanin-Sensitive Magnetic Resonance Imaging and (18)F-Fluorodopa-Positron Emission Tomography.
evidence.snippet: High-LR PAF patients showed reduced contrast in the LC and SN compared with controls and low-LR PAF patients, with values similar to PD and DLB.
